events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte Proclaimed Emperor of the French
events.description: The French Senate adopted a constitutional act naming Napoleon Bonaparte Emperor of the French. The change turned the Consulate into an imperial monarchy, only a little over a decade after the Revolution had toppled the Bourbon crown.
events.significance: It launched the Napoleonic Empire, which redrew the map of Europe and spread legal reforms such as the Napoleonic Code.

events.title: Plessy v. Ferguson Upholds 'Separate but Equal'
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 7–1 that racial segregation in public facilities was constitutional, provided the separate facilities were nominally equal. The case began when Homer Plessy deliberately challenged Louisiana's segregated railway car law.
events.significance: The decision gave legal cover to Jim Crow segregation for nearly six decades, until Brown v. Board of Education overturned the doctrine in 1954.

events.title: Birth of Karol Wojtyła, the Future Pope John Paul II
events.description: Karol Józef Wojtyła was born in Wadowice, Poland. He became Pope in 1978, the first non-Italian pontiff in 455 years.
events.significance: His long papacy shaped late 20th-century world affairs, and he is widely credited with inspiring the movements that helped end communist rule in Eastern Europe.

events.title: India Conducts 'Smiling Buddha' Nuclear Test
events.description: India detonated its first nuclear device in the Pokhran desert of Rajasthan. The test was code-named 'Smiling Buddha'.
events.significance: India became the sixth country with nuclear weapons, which changed the strategic balance in South Asia and fueled global debate over nonproliferation.

events.title: Mount St. Helens Erupts
events.description: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake triggered a massive eruption of Mount St. Helens in Washington State. The north face of the mountain collapsed in the largest landslide in recorded history, followed by a devastating blast.
events.significance: It was the deadliest and most economically destructive volcanic event in U.S. history, and it transformed how scientists monitor and study volcanoes.
